name: musbotg_dev_ctrl_data_rx
prose: Device-mode control transfer OUT data stage receive for the MUSB controller; static uint8_t, 0 means complete and 1 not complete. It selects endpoint 0, writes any pending sc->sc_ep0_cmd to TXCSRL and clears it, then reads TXCSRL. If SETUPEND or SENTSTALL is set it returns 0, with no error when td->remainder is 0 (a complete transfer followed by the next SETUP) and with td->error = 1 otherwise. If RXPKTRDY is not set it returns 1. Otherwise it reads the byte count; a count below td->max_frame_size marks a short packet (td->short_pkt = 1 and a local got_short), a count above it sets td->error = 1 and returns 0; a count greater than td->remainder also sets td->error = 1 and returns 0. It copies the bytes from the FIFO into the transfer's pages (through the bounce buffer when the destination is not 4-byte aligned), reducing remainder and advancing offset. Finally, if td->remainder is 0 or this packet was short: when td->short_pkt is set it stores MUSB2_MASK_CSR0L_RXPKTRDY_CLR in sc->sc_ep0_cmd (to be written on the next call) and returns 0; when td->short_pkt is not set (remainder reached 0 on a full-size packet) it falls to the common tail. The common tail writes RXPKTRDY_CLR to TXCSRL immediately and returns 1, so a full-size final packet leaves the transfer not complete (a zero-length packet is still expected).
note: musb_otg.c:633-770. Reviewer original right (returns 1 when remainder is 0 without a short packet, 759-770); round 15 right (the deferred RXPKTRDY_CLR is queued whenever short_pkt is set in the remainder==0-or-got_short case, 759-763, not only when remainder is 0). Returns 667, 673, 676, 690, 697, 763, 770.

name: ohci_non_isoc_done
prose: Completes a non-isochronous OHCI transfer; static void. It starts with err = 0 and td_transfer_cache = td_transfer_first. For a control transfer with a header stage it runs ohci_non_isoc_done_sub (storing its result in err), sets aframes to 1 (without incrementing it per call here) and jumps to done if the transfer descriptor cache became NULL. It then loops while aframes != nframes: err = ohci_non_isoc_done_sub(xfer), aframes++, and a jump to done when the cache became NULL. For a control transfer whose data stage is not active (control_act clear) it runs one more ohci_non_isoc_done_sub for the status stage, again overwriting err. At done it calls ohci_device_done(xfer, err). err is overwritten by each sub-scan, not aggregated, so the error of an earlier stage is lost when a later scan runs; the status-stage scan does not increment aframes.
note: ohci.c:891-932. Reviewer original right (err overwritten, 910, 919, 929); round 15 right (aframes is set to 1 after the control header scan and is not incremented around the final status scan, 912, 927-929). Not read: ohci_non_isoc_done_sub semantics beyond its listing (799-887), ohci_device_done.

name: xhci_configure_reset_endpoint
prose: Re-initializes an endpoint on the xHCI controller after its transfer ring was reset; static usb_error_t. It derives the endpoint id from the descriptor (a control endpoint is treated as direction IN) and returns USB_ERR_NO_PIPE if the id is 0. It takes the command lock and calls xhci_configure_endpoint_by_xfer; if that fails it unlocks and returns that error. It then gets the endpoint into the stopped state according to its state: Disabled or Stopped needs nothing (drop = 0); Halted sends a reset-endpoint command and sets drop when it fails; any other state sends a stop-endpoint command and sets drop when it fails. It then sends set-TR-dequeue-pointer for the stream with the endpoint's ring address (a failure is only logged). Only when drop is set and the endpoint type is neither control nor isochronous does it configure a drop (xhci_configure_mask and configure-endpoint command), clearing the endpoint's bit in ep_configured on success (a failure is only logged). It then configures the slot and endpoint context: when the endpoint's bit in ep_configured is clear it sends a configure-endpoint command and sets the bit if that succeeded, otherwise it sends an evaluate-context command; a failure is only logged. It unlocks the command lock and returns 0 (USB_ERR_NORMAL_COMPLETION) in all those cases: errors from the stop, reset, dequeue-pointer and configure commands are not returned.
note: xhci.c:3846-3978. Reviewer original right (returns 0 despite command failures; ep_configured and dequeue pointer not guaranteed, 3924-3930, 3964-3978); round 15 right (the drop/re-add happens only when the reset or stop command failed, `drop != 0`, 3944). Returns 3882, 3892, 3978.

name: fg_add_new_strokes
prose: Creates new strokes from the unmatched pressure spans of one sensor frame in the atp touchpad driver; static void. It copies the spans whose matched flag is false from pspans_x and pspans_y into local arrays and counts them (nspans[X], nspans[Y]). If the two counts are equal it adds one stroke per index pair with fg_add_stroke(spans[X][i], spans[Y][i]). Otherwise the axis with fewer unmatched spans is the repeat axis (repeat_axis = (nspans[X] > nspans[Y]) ? Y : X), repeat_count is the absolute difference of the counts, and on that axis it picks the span with the largest cumulative pressure (repeat_index). It then pairs spans index by index with fg_add_stroke until either axis runs out, and while repeat_count > 0 it repeats the span at repeat_index (decrementing the loop index of the repeat axis) at most repeat_count additional times, so that the repeated span is paired with exactly enough spans of the other axis to make up the difference, not with every span of the other axis. fg_add_stroke allocates a stroke with atp_alloc_stroke and returns without adding one when none is available.
note: atp.c:1711-1771 (fg_add_stroke at 1667). Reviewer original right (the repeated span is on the axis with fewer spans, 1743); round 15 right (the repeat count is the count difference, 1744, 1758-1767).

name: ukbd_read_char_locked
prose: Reads one keyboard character or scan code from the USB keyboard (locked variant); returns an int32/uint32 code, NOKEY or ERRKEY. Precondition: the keyboard lock is held (UKBD_LOCK_ASSERT). It returns NOKEY if the keyboard is not active. At next_code, if a composed character is pending and the compose flag is not set it returns that character, after clearing sc_composed_char, as ERRKEY when it is above 0xFF. With UKBD_EMULATE_ATSCANCODE and K_RAW mode it first returns buffered scan codes (an E0/E1 prefix first). Otherwise it fetches a key with ukbd_get_key (blocking when wait is true): -1 gives NOKEY; any real key increments kbd->kb_count, even if the following translation yields no key. The usb code is translated to a keycode (AT scancode emulation or the translation table); NN gives NOKEY. In K_RAW mode it returns the scan code or usb code. A left-alt (0x38) key press sets the compose flag and clears the composed char, and its release clears the flag and, if sc_composed_char is above 0xFF, resets it to 0. K_CODE mode returns the keycode (with the release bit for releases). In compose mode the keypad digit keys accumulate decimal digits in sc_composed_char (releases of those keys continue with the next key; an overflow past 0xFF continues to next_code), and any other key while sc_composed_char > 0 clears the compose flag and the composed char and returns ERRKEY. Otherwise genkbd_keyaction translates the key; NOKEY continues with the next key (goto next_code), else the action is returned.
note: ukbd.c:1677-1852. Reviewer original right (compose/alt state updates and NOKEY conditions omitted by old annotation); round 2 right (kb_count incremented at 1730 even when mapping yields NN/NOKEY); round 15 wrong in effect: the code clears sc_composed_char when composed char > 0xFF (1699, 1763). check_composed: if sc_composed_char <= 0xFF it goes to next_code (1846-1848), otherwise errkey (ERRKEY) at 1850-1851. Not read: ukbd_get_key, genkbd_keyaction.

name: ums_intr_callback
prose: USB interrupt-transfer callback of the ums mouse driver; static void. It gets the transfer length with usbd_xfer_status. In USB_ST_TRANSFERRED: it truncates len to sizeof(sc_temp); a zero length goes to tr_setup; it copies the data out, takes the report id from the first byte when sc_iid is set (reducing len) or, for UMS_FLAG_SBU devices without report ids, ignores packets whose first byte is 0x14 or 0x15 (goto tr_setup). For each ums_info it accumulates the w, x, y, z, t axis deltas and the button bits that appear in the report, keeps button bits not found in the report from the previous state, and if any delta is non-zero or the buttons differ from sc_status.button it updates sc_status (button, dx, dy, dz; t is not exported) and, for an SBU device with an all-zero report, only arms a 50 ms callout, else stops the callout, queues the event with ums_put_queue and (with EVDEV_SUPPORT) pushes it with ums_evdev_push. With a report in which the wheel axis t is non-zero it first queues the previous button state and sets button bits 5 or 6. If there was no change nothing is queued. It then falls through to USB_ST_SETUP (tr_setup), which, when the receive FIFO has no room (usb_fifo_put_bytes_max == 0) and no evdev client is open (or EVDEV_SUPPORT is not built), breaks without resubmitting; otherwise it sets the frame length to the maximum and submits the transfer. In the error default case, a cancelled transfer does nothing; any other error sets the stall and goes to tr_setup, so it is resubmitted unless the same FIFO-full condition applies.
note: ums.c:218-401. Reviewer original right (no change -> nothing queued; resubmit is conditional on FIFO room or an open evdev client, 380-391); round 15 right (the error path resubmits only through tr_setup and may break when the FIFO is full and evdev is closed). Not read: ums_put_queue, ums_evdev_push, hid_get_data.

name: usbhid_intr_out_callback
prose: USB interrupt-OUT transfer callback of the usbhid driver; static void. For USB_ST_TRANSFERRED and USB_ST_SETUP it takes len = xfer_ctx->req.intr.maxlen. If len is 0: in polling mode (USB_IN_POLLING_MODE_FUNC) it sets xfer_ctx->error to 0; in all cases it returns without calling the callback. Otherwise it copies len bytes from xfer_ctx->buf into the transfer's frame, sets the frame length, submits the transfer, sets req.intr.maxlen to 0 and, in polling mode, returns; otherwise it sets xfer_ctx->error to 0 and calls the completion callback xfer_ctx->cb(xfer_ctx) (ignoring its result), so the callback is also called after a successful non-polling submission. In the error case: an error other than USB_ERR_CANCELLED sets the stall and retries from the setup code; USB_ERR_CANCELLED sets xfer_ctx->error to EIO and calls the callback, also in polling mode.
note: usbhid.c:152-189 (slice 1-257 is the file head; the callback is at 152). Reviewer original right (callback also runs on successful non-polling completion path, 175-186); round 15 right (the cancelled-error path calls the callback even in polling mode, 184-186). Not read: cb implementations.

name: uled_ioctl
prose: ioctl handler of the uled USB LED device; returns 0 or an errno. It takes the softc mutex (sc_mtx) and switches on cmd. ULED_GET_COLOR copies the stored sc_color into *addr (it writes the caller's structure) and returns 0. ULED_SET_COLOR reads the colour from *addr, stores red, green and blue in sc->sc_color before sending anything (so the stored colour changes even if the USB request fails), builds an 8-byte report (for ULED_FLAG_BLINK1 devices: 0x01, 'n', red, green, blue and zeros; otherwise red, green, blue, three zeros, 0x1a, 0x05) and sends it with uled_ctrl_msg as a class interface SET_REPORT request (value 0x200); the result of uled_ctrl_msg is the return value. Any other command returns ENOTTY. The mutex is released before returning.
note: uled.c:243-290 (slice 252-291 starts inside; name correct). Reviewer round 15 right (GET writes *addr and SET only reads it). Returns 290 (single). Not read: uled_ctrl_msg.

name: mos_bulk_write_callback
prose: USB bulk-OUT (transmit) callback of the mos Ethernet driver; static void. In USB_ST_TRANSFERRED it increments IFCOUNTER_OPACKETS by 1 and then continues into the setup code. In USB_ST_SETUP (and after a completed transfer) it dequeues one mbuf from the interface send queue; if there is none it returns without submitting anything. Otherwise it copies the frame into the transfer's first frame, sets the frame length to m_pkthdr.len, passes a copy to BPF (BPF_MTAP), frees the mbuf, submits the transfer, increments IFCOUNTER_OPACKETS again at submit time (so a completed transfer followed by another queued packet is counted twice, once at completion and once at the new submission) and returns. On a USB error it increments IFCOUNTER_OERRORS; if the error is not USB_ERR_CANCELLED it sets the stall and retries through the setup code, else it returns.
note: if_mos.c:839-886. Reviewer original right (if_dequeue returning NULL returns without resubmitting, 857-858); round 15 right that the SETUP path alone increments once (875), though TRANSFERRED adds the completion increment at 849, so the old prose about two increments per path was partly right. Returns 858, 876, 884.

name: umb_up
prose: Advances the MBIM modem's bring-up state machine by one step; static void. It switches on sc->sc_state: UMB_S_DOWN calls umb_open; UMB_S_OPEN, when UMBFLG_FCC_AUTH_REQUIRED is set: with sc_cid == -1 calls umb_allocate_cid and leaves the switch; with a CID already allocated calls umb_newstate(sc, UMB_S_CID, UMB_NS_DONT_DROP) and then falls into the UMB_S_CID case, which calls umb_send_fcc_auth (so two actions in that case); without the flag it calls umb_radio(sc, 1); UMB_S_CID calls umb_send_fcc_auth; UMB_S_RADIO sends a subscriber-ready-status query; UMB_S_SIMREADY calls umb_packet_service(sc, 1); UMB_S_ATTACHED resets sc_tx_seq to 0 and calls umb_connect; UMB_S_CONNECTED calls umb_qry_ipconfig; UMB_S_UP only, if IFF_DRV_RUNNING is not yet set, sets it, clears IFF_DRV_OACTIVE and calls umb_rx(sc); it does not start any other state-advancing action. After the switch (including after the allocate-CID break) it re-arms sc_statechg_timer with umb_statechg_timeout when sc_state is still below UMB_S_UP, and stops that timer otherwise. Returns void.
note: if_umb.c:1093-1153. Reviewer original right (UMB_S_UP issues no state-advancing action; the FCC-auth case falls through issuing two actions, 1103-1119); round 15 right (the allocate-CID path `break`s out of the switch and then arms the timer, 1104-1107, 1147-1149).

name: uhub_reattach_port
prose: Re-enumerates the device on a hub port; static usb_error_t, 0 on success or the error of a failed control request. It first clears UHF_C_PORT_CONNECTION on the port (an error goes to the error label), frees any existing child device on the port with usb_free_device and re-reads the port status (an error goes to the error label). With USB_HAVE_DISABLE_ENUM, if enumeration is disabled globally or for this hub it goes to the error label with err still 0; if the port has no connected device it also goes to the error label with err 0 (nothing is reset and no speed is determined). Otherwise, when the port is in host mode it clears a still-set suspend feature, waits for the power-up delay, resets the port with usbd_req_reset_port (an error is logged and goes to the error label), re-reads the status, and if the connect-change bit is set or the device is no longer connected it repeats the whole sequence once (timeout flag) and on the second occurrence gives up through the error label with err 0. It then derives the device speed from the hub's speed and the port status bits (for a SuperSpeed hub with U1/U2 timeouts it calls usbd_req_set_hub_u1_timeout and usbd_req_set_hub_u2_timeout, whose errors are only logged and do not change the return value), chooses the device mode and allocates the child with usb_alloc_device; if that returns NULL it goes to the error label, otherwise it returns 0. The error label frees a child device if one exists; when err is 0 and the port status shows the port enabled it clears UHF_PORT_ENABLE with usbd_req_clear_port_feature (so the no-device and enumeration-disabled exits do clear port enable when it was set), logs 'device problem' with the error code if there is one, and returns err.
note: usb_hub.c:599-841 (slice 514-798 starts earlier). Reviewer original right (returns 0 without resetting or determining speed when nothing is connected or enumeration is disabled, 643-652); round 15 mixed: right that the U1/U2 errors are only logged (783-797, return 0 at 819), wrong that the no-device branch never clears port-enable (829-834 clears it when the port is enabled). Returns 819, 840. Not read: usbd_req_* bodies.

name: usb_do_clear_stall_callback
prose: USB transfer callback that clears the halt condition of stalled endpoints, one at a time; static void. It takes the USB bus lock itself on entry and releases it before returning (it drops and retakes it around usbd_transfer_submit). It starts from udev->ep_curr. In USB_ST_TRANSFERRED it resets clear_stall_errors to 0 and, unless ep_curr is NULL (device unconfigured, which goes to the setup code), for an endpoint that has a descriptor and is marked stalled it clears toggle_next and is_stalled, calls usbd_clear_stall_locked and restarts the pending transfer of every stream queue, then advances to the next endpoint and falls into USB_ST_SETUP. In SETUP, if the device has no endpoints it does nothing; otherwise it wraps the endpoint pointer to the first endpoint when out of range and scans forward (at most endpoints_max positions) for the next endpoint with a descriptor that is stalled; for that endpoint it builds a CLEAR_FEATURE(ENDPOINT_HALT) device request for its address, sets one frame and submits the transfer, and stops scanning. At exit, udev->ep_curr is set to the endpoint last examined (the stalled endpoint just submitted, not the next one). On an error: a cancelled transfer does nothing; otherwise, unless usb_no_cs_fail is set or the error is USB_ERR_STALLED (both treated as success, so the stalled endpoint is cleared locally), it counts the failure: a timeout re-enumerates the device and sets clear_stall_errors to USB_CS_RESET_LIMIT, other errors increment the counter and re-enumerate when it reaches the limit; it then retries through the setup code, which does nothing further when the counter is at the limit.
note: usb_request.c:272-391. Reviewer original right (it calls USB_BUS_LOCK itself, 284, 391); round 15 right (ep_curr is the stalled endpoint just submitted, 344, 390, and failures treated as success clear the stall state locally, 360-370). Not read: usbd_clear_stall_locked, usb_command_wrapper.

name: usbd_do_request_flags
prose: Performs a USB control request on a device and waits for completion; returns a usb_error_t. The timeout is clamped to 50..30000 ms. It returns USB_ERR_NOT_CONFIGURED if the device state is below USB_STATE_POWERED and zeroes *actlen if non-NULL. Without USB_HAVE_USER_IO a request with USB_USER_DATA_PTR returns USB_ERR_INVAL at once (before it touches the caller's mutex). If mtx is non-NULL and not Giant it unlocks it (and it is relocked at done). It takes the control-transfer serialization lock (usbd_ctrl_lock). If the device has a handle-request function (device mode or a root hub) it uses it instead of a transfer: a write with non-zero length gives USB_ERR_INVAL; the function's error is returned; a returned descriptor shorter than the requested length gives USB_ERR_SHORT_XFER (with *actlen left at 0 and nothing copied) unless USB_SHORT_XFER_OK is set, in which case the length is cut to what was returned; the data are copied to the caller (copyout failure gives USB_ERR_INVAL), *actlen is set and it goes to done. Otherwise it sets up the control transfer (USB_ERR_NOMEM if it cannot), sets the manual-status and short-transfer flags from flags and the timeout, copies the setup packet into frame 0 and loops: each pass sets the data frame length (at most the transfer maximum), copies write data in, starts the transfer and waits for completion (cv_wait), takes xfer->error, copies read data out, advances the data pointer, updates *actlen and stops at an error, a timeout (USB_ERR_TIMEOUT when the elapsed time exceeds the timeout), or when no data remains. On error it stops the transfer. At done it releases the control lock if it took it, relocks the caller's mutex and, for any error other than normal completion, short transfer, stall or cancel, sleeps hz/16 for transaction-translator cleanup before returning the error.
note: usb_request.c:461-784. Reviewer round 15 right on both points (the USB_USER_DATA_PTR rejection returns before the mutex is touched, 510-512; a short descriptor without SHORT_XFER_OK returns USB_ERR_SHORT_XFER before setting *actlen or copying, 550-553). PARTLY READ: the debug-only (USB_REQ_DEBUG) lines 621-640 and the manual status-stage handling (660-684) were read only superficially.

name: usbd_req_reset_port
prose: Resets a hub port and waits for the reset to finish; returns a usb_error_t. It first tries to clear UHF_C_PORT_RESET (any error is ignored), then sets UHF_PORT_RESET (an error is returned). It then polls: pause usb_port_reset_delay ms, add that to a counter n, read the port status (an error is returned); if the port is no longer connected it returns the current err value, which is 0, so a vanished device is reported as success; if the reset-change bit is set it leaves the loop; if the reset bit is no longer asserted (a VM workaround) it leaves the loop; if n exceeds 1000 ms it sets n to 0 and leaves the loop. After the loop it clears UHF_C_PORT_RESET again and returns that error if nonzero (so a failed clear after a timeout returns the clear error, not USB_ERR_TIMEOUT); then it returns USB_ERR_TIMEOUT if n is 0 (the wait timed out). Otherwise it pauses usb_port_reset_recovery ms and returns 0.
note: usb_request.c:842-915. Reviewer original right (returns 0 when the device disappears, 876-877); round 15 right (the first clear-port-feature error is ignored, 853-854; a failure of the second clear returns that error before the timeout check, 899-907).

name: usbd_req_warm_reset_port
prose: Performs a warm (BH) reset on a SuperSpeed hub port; returns a usb_error_t. It reads the port status (an error is returned). Only when the link state is U3, compliance mode, loopback or SS.Inactive does it continue; for any other link state it logs and returns 0 without doing anything. It tries to clear UHF_C_BH_PORT_RESET (error ignored), sets UHF_BH_PORT_RESET (error returned), then polls the status every usb_port_reset_delay ms: a status read error is returned; if the device is no longer connected it returns the current err, which is 0; if the BH reset change bit is set it leaves the loop; if the accumulated wait n exceeds 1000 ms it sets n to 0 and leaves. After the loop it clears UHF_C_BH_PORT_RESET and returns that error if nonzero (so that error wins over a timeout), then returns USB_ERR_TIMEOUT if n is 0, else pauses usb_port_reset_recovery ms and returns 0.
note: usb_request.c:932-1014. Reviewer original right (returns 0 when the device disappears, 983-984); round 15 right (initial clear error ignored 961-962; the clear failure after the loop is returned before the timeout, 998-1006). The early return 0 for wrong link states at 957 is not mentioned by the reviewers.

name: usbd_callback_wrapper
prose: Runs the callback of the transfer at the head of a transfer queue (the 'done' queue command); static void. Precondition: the USB bus lock is held. If the queue is being recursed (recurse_3 != 0) or the transfer's xfer_mtx is not owned by the caller, and the system is not in polling mode, it postpones the work by signalling the done process (usb_proc_msignal) and returns, still holding the bus lock. Otherwise it clears done_q.curr, sets doing_callback, drops the bus lock and then: if the transfer is not transferring it sets usb_state to USB_ST_SETUP and, if it was not started, retakes the bus lock and goes to done without calling the callback; if it is transferring it calls usbd_callback_wrapper_sub(xfer); a nonzero result retakes the bus lock and goes to done without calling the callback; otherwise it releases the power reference (USB_HAVE_POWERD), clears transferring, sets usb_state to USB_ST_ERROR or USB_ST_TRANSFERRED and syncs DMA after a successful transfer. It then (with USB_HAVE_PF) taps the transfer when the state is not SETUP and calls xfer->callback(xfer, xfer->error). It retakes the bus lock; if the transfer is not open, is started and the state is USB_ST_ERROR (it was started after being cancelled) it clears doing_callback, requeues the transfer on done_q with usb_command_wrapper and returns without the drain check. At done it clears doing_callback, and if the transfer is draining and not transferring it clears draining and broadcasts cv_drain, then runs the next queued command with usb_command_wrapper(&info->done_q, info->done_q.curr) and returns.
note: usb_transfer.c:2395-2520. Reviewer original right (no-callback path when not started or when wrapper_sub returns nonzero; drain wake only when draining, 2442-2453, 2510-2515); round 15 right (the 'started after cancel' requeue path returns before the drain check, 2493-2500, and requires !open rather than 'reopened').

name: usbd_callback_wrapper_sub
prose: Post-processes a transfer before its callback is called; static uint8_t returning 1 to wait for a new callback or 0 to call the callback now. If the transfer is not open and not yet closed it calls the endpoint's close method under the bus lock, sets did_close and returns 1. If xfer->error is non-zero, the DMA delay has not been done, and the error is USB_ERR_CANCELLED or USB_ERR_TIMEOUT or the bus has a start_dma_delay method (so any error when that method exists), it sets did_dma_delay, clears can_cancel_immed, gets the DMA delay for the device and, when it is non-zero, starts the bus's DMA-delay handler or a timeout calling usb_dma_delay_done_cb and returns 1. It then limits aframes to nframes (panicking only if the error is 0), sums frlengths into actlen, zeroes the length of frames not transferred, and limits actlen to sumlen (panicking only if the error is 0). If there is an error it clears control_act, requests a TT buffer reset for errors other than normal completion, short transfer, stall or cancel (USB_HAVE_TT_SUPPORT), and for a non-cancel error on a pipe_bof transfer jumps to done and returns 0 without starting the next transfer. Without an error: a short actual length clears control_act and, when short transfers are not allowed, sets xfer->error to USB_ERR_SHORT_XFER (jumping to done and returning 0 for pipe_bof); a full-length transfer in the middle of an active control transfer (control_act) jumps to done and returns 0. Otherwise, if this transfer is the current one of its endpoint queue (stream_id), it runs the queue's command to start the next transfer and, when the queue is empty, clears the endpoint's is_synced flag. It returns 0.
note: usb_transfer.c:2963-3139. Reviewer original right (returns 0 through done without starting the next transfer on pipe_bof or active control transfer, 3084-3088, 3110-3113); round 15 right (the DMA-delay branch condition includes `bus->methods->start_dma_delay != NULL`, 2985-2988, so it is not limited to non-hardware errors). Returns 2979, 3018, 3139. PARTLY READ: 3128-3136 (queue-empty branch).

name: usbd_xfer_get_isochronous_start_frame
prose: Computes the next isochronous frame number at which the first packet of a transfer should be queued and updates the endpoint's schedule; uint8_t, returning non-zero when a discontinuity occurred and 0 in normal operation. delta = (endpoint->isoc_next - frame_curr) & frame_mask. If the endpoint is not synced (is_synced == 0), or delta is smaller than frame_ms + frame_min, or delta is larger than frame_mask / 2 (a negative delta), it resets isoc_next to (frame_curr + 2 * frame_ms + frame_min) & frame_mask, sets is_synced to 1 and returns 1; otherwise it returns 0. If p_frame_start is non-NULL it stores isoc_next & frame_mask in it (after the possible reset). It then computes the frame offset delta again (in units of frame_ms, with the current frame rounded down), selects shift = 3 for a full-speed device and usbd_xfer_get_fps_shift(xfer) otherwise, computes duration = ((nframes << shift) + 7) / 8, sets xfer->isoc_time_complete to the expanded current time plus the delta plus the duration, advances endpoint->isoc_next by duration * frame_ms (masked with frame_mask) and returns the retval computed above.
note: usb_transfer.c:3693-3752 (packet name usbd_isoc_start does not exist; real name usbd_xfer_get_isochronous_start_frame). Returns 3751 only. Not read: usb_isoc_time_expand, usbd_xfer_get_fps_shift.

name: mtw_fw_callback
prose: USB bulk-OUT callback used to download firmware to the MediaTek mtw chip, one chunk at a time; static void. It clears the transfer's private pointer. USB_ST_TRANSFERRED: adds actlen to sc->sc_sent and zeroes the first actlen bytes of the current firmware buffer txd_fw[sc_idx]; if actlen is below 0x2c44 and sc_idx is 0 it returns without submitting anything; if sc_idx is 3 it writes the interrupt vector block (mtw_write_ivb, logging a failure), waits 10 ms and polls the MCU DMA address register up to 100 times (10 ms apart) for MTW_MCU_READY: when ready it sets fwloading to 1 and stops polling, if the 100 tries are used up it sets fwloading to 0; it then wakes up waiters on fwloading and returns; otherwise if actlen equals 0x2c44 it increments sc_idx and delays 1 ms, and then continues into USB_ST_SETUP. USB_ST_SETUP: takes dlen from the length field of txd_fw[sc_idx], writes the MCU DMA address (0x40 + sc_sent) and length registers, sets frame 0 to the firmware buffer with length dlen and submits the transfer. On an error it prints a message, sets fwloading to 0 and wakes waiters; it does not resubmit. It returns void.
note: if_mtw.c:2841-2927 (the packet name mtw_bulk_tx_callbackN is a different function at 2703; the slice 2855-3119 starts inside mtw_fw_callback and also includes mtw_bulk_tx_callback0-5 and mtw_set_tx_desc, so the prose is for mtw_fw_callback as the reviewers' notes about txd_fw/sc_idx/fwloading describe). Reviewer original right (short idx0 returns early, 2859-2860); round 15 right (the code handles firmware loading, not the data TX queue). The data TX callback mtw_bulk_tx_callbackN (2703-2839) was not described by this item. Not read: mtw_write_ivb, mtw_read_cfg.

name: mtw_vap_create
prose: Creates a net80211 vap for the mtw driver; returns the vap or NULL. It returns NULL (after a message) if sc->rvp_cnt is already at or above MTW_VAP_MAX. For IEEE80211_M_STA (also adding IEEE80211_CLONE_NOBEACONS), IBSS, monitor, hostap and mesh modes it returns NULL if the interface already has any vap; for WDS it needs an existing hostap vap (clearing the clone-BSSID flag) and otherwise returns NULL with a message; any other mode prints a message and returns NULL. It allocates the mtw_vap (M_WAITOK, zeroed) and calls ieee80211_vap_setup, freeing it and returning NULL if that fails. It then sets iv_update_beacon, iv_max_aid, the RX A-MPDU limit (both branches choose the 64K value) and density, the key set and delete hooks, saves the original iv_newstate in rvp->newstate and installs mtw_newstate (for IBSS it also hooks iv_recv_mgmt), initializes rate control (1 s interval) and calls ieee80211_vap_attach. It then takes the first free index of sc->rvp_bmap as rvp_id, increments rvp_cnt (setting ic_opmode to the mode for the first vap), sets cmdq_run to MTW_CMDQ_GO for hostap and returns the vap.
note: if_mtw.c:746-857 (slice 761-1016 starts inside; name correct). Reviewer round 15 wrong: rvp_cnt >= MTW_VAP_MAX is checked at 756-758 and returns NULL. Returns 758, 772, 785, 790, 800, 857.

name: rsu_rx_event
prose: Handles a firmware event received by the rsu driver; static void with the event code, buffer and length. It uses the first vap of the interface, which may be NULL. R92S_EVT_SURVEY calls rsu_event_survey. R92S_EVT_SURVEY_DONE logs and: if sc_extra_scan is 1 it clears it and, when a vap exists and rsu_site_survey(sc, NULL) fails, drops the lock and cancels the scan (ieee80211_cancel_scan) and in any case then ends the case without calling scan_done; otherwise, when a vap exists, it drops the lock and calls ieee80211_scan_done(vap); with a NULL vap it does nothing further. R92S_EVT_JOIN_BSS calls rsu_event_join_bss only when vap->iv_state is IEEE80211_S_AUTH (vap is dereferenced without a NULL check). R92S_EVT_DEL_STA logs and, when the vap is in RUN state and the event's address equals the BSS id, drops the lock and moves the vap to IEEE80211_S_SCAN (also dereferencing vap unchecked). R92S_EVT_WPS_PBC only logs; R92S_EVT_FWDBG terminates the buffer at byte 60 and logs it; R92S_EVT_ADDBA_REQ_REPORT calls rsu_event_addba_req_report; any other code prints 'unhandled code'.
note: if_rsu.c:2179-2240 (slice 2075-2328 starts earlier). Reviewer original right (JOIN_BSS only runs in AUTH, the default has no handler, vap may be NULL, 2212, 2219); round 15 right (SURVEY_DONE does nothing when vap is NULL, 2205-2210; the survey case omitted by the old annotation). Not read: the rsu_event_* helper bodies beyond join_bss.

name: rum_newstate
prose: net80211 state-change method for a rum vap; static int. Precondition: the caller holds the net80211 com lock; the function releases it, takes the driver lock, and retakes the com lock before returning. It stops the rate-control callout. If leaving IEEE80211_S_SLEEP in station mode it clears the ACK/CTS power-management and auto-wakeup bits and sets power state 0 (errors ignored). Then by new state: INIT aborts the TSF sync if the old state was RUN; RUN (unless it comes from SLEEP, already handled) refs the BSS node and, for non-monitor vaps, fails with EINVAL when the BSS channel or the node channel is IEEE80211_CHAN_ANYC, otherwise updates slot time, MRR, TX preamble, basic rates and max retry and sets the BSSID; for hostap and IBSS it calls rum_alloc_beacon (nonzero result becomes the return value and ends the case); for non-monitor, non-ahdemo vaps it calls rum_enable_tsf_sync (a nonzero result is likewise returned), else rum_enable_tsf; when the channel's unicast rate is not fixed it starts rate control; SLEEP, for station vaps only, sets the auto-wakeup and ACK/CTS power-management bits (a USB error gives EIO) and calls rum_set_power_state(sc, 1) whose nonzero result is returned. It then releases the driver lock, retakes the com lock and returns ret if non-zero, else the result of the saved rvp->newstate(vap, nstate, arg).
note: if_rum.c:958-1066. Reviewer original right (it drops the com lock itself, so the caller must hold it on entry, 974, 1065); round 15 right (RUN can fail with the rum_alloc_beacon and rum_enable_tsf_sync results, 1019-1026, not only EINVAL/EIO).

name: urtw_8187b_cmd_reset
prose: Resets the RTL8187B command register block; static usb_error_t. It reads URTW_CMD, keeps bit 0x2 and sets URTW_CMD_RST, writes it back, then polls up to 20 times (2 ms pause each) reading URTW_CMD until the reset bit clears; if it is still set after 20 tries it prints 'reset timeout'. The register accessors set the local error variable and jump to the fail label on a USB error, and the fail label returns error. The function therefore returns the error of the last register access: the USB error code if a read or write failed, and the value of the last successful access (0) otherwise, so the reset timeout case also returns 0 (the message is only printed).
note: if_urtw.c:1289-1312. Reviewer original right (never returns an explicit error for the timeout), round 15 right (error holds the last access result, which is 0 after a successful read; urtw_read8_m/urtw_write8_m assign error and goto fail only on nonzero, 131-140).

name: vge_attach
prose: Attach routine of the VIA Velocity (vge) Ethernet driver; returns 0 or an errno. It initializes the softc mutex and watchdog callout, maps the memory BAR (ENXIO if it cannot), looks up the PCI Express and power-management capabilities, tries to allocate a single MSI (falling back to INTx), allocates the IRQ (ENXIO if it cannot), resets the chip, waits up to VGE_TIMEOUT iterations for the EEPROM reload bit to clear, reads the station address from the EEPROM, allocates the DMA resources with vge_dma_alloc (an error goes to fail), sets up the ifnet, attaches the PHY with mii_attach (an error goes to fail), calls ether_ifattach and sets up the interrupt handler with bus_setup_intr (an error goes to fail). Every failure reaches the fail label, which, when error is non-zero, calls vge_detach(dev) to release whatever was acquired so far, and then returns the error; vge_detach checks each resource before releasing it, but it does not free the sysctl nodes created earlier in attach.
note: if_vge.c:993-1145 (packet name correct; slice 1022-1276 starts inside and ends in vge_newbuf). Reviewer round 15 right that vge_detach (1156-1196) does not release sysctl nodes; the exact sysctl creation point was not located (SYSCTL_ADD lines not found in the 993-1145 skeleton, they may be created in a helper). PARTLY READ: 1022-1130 only through control-flow lines.

name: vge_poll
prose: DEVICE_POLLING handler of the vge driver; returns the number of received packets from the first receive pass (rx_npkts). It takes the softc lock. If IFF_DRV_RUNNING is not set it goes to done and returns 0. Otherwise it runs vge_rxeof(sc, count) (its result is the return value), vge_txeof, and vge_start_locked when the send queue is non-empty. For cmd == POLL_AND_CHECK_STATUS it reads VGE_ISR: a value of 0xFFFFFFFF goes to done; a non-zero status is written back to VGE_ISR to acknowledge it (a zero status is not written); a TX or RX DMA stall clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING and re-initializes the chip with vge_init_locked; an RX overflow or no-descriptor status runs a second vge_rxeof(sc, count), whose packet count is ignored (not added to the return value) and restarts the receive queue. It unlocks and returns rx_npkts.
note: if_vge.c:1692-1733 (compiled only with DEVICE_POLLING). Reviewer original and round 2 right (the second vge_rxeof result is ignored, 1726); round 15 right (the ISR write happens only if status != 0, 1712-1713). Returns 1733 only.

name: edid_parse
prose: Parses a 128-byte EDID block into a struct edid_info; int, returns 0 on success or -1. It returns -1 without writing anything if edid_is_valid(data) returns non-zero (invalid EDID). Otherwise it fills the vendor id string, product id, vendor and product names (from the lookup tables, or empty strings), the serial number string, manufacture week and year, EDID version and revision, video input, maximum horizontal and vertical size, gamma, features, the chromaticity coordinates (note that ec_redy is assigned EDID_CHROMA_REDX(data), not REDY, so the red-y value is wrong), and the extension block count. It builds the mode list: the established timings (looked up in the standard mode list), the standard timings (each not already present), and the detailed timing and descriptor blocks with edid_block, trims trailing whitespace from the name, serial and comment strings, computes the maximum pixel clock over the modes and, when the monitor has range limits, raises er_max_clock to cover it, and returns 0.
note: edid.c:509-641 (packet slice 538-642 starts inside; name correct). Reviewer round 15 right (ec_redy uses EDID_CHROMA_REDX, 562-563); round 17 right (the validity check returns -1 when edid_is_valid is non-zero, 518-519, old prose said nonzero). Returns 519, 641. PARTLY READ: edid_block, mode lookup bodies not read.

name: vmd_attach
prose: Attach routine of the Intel VMD (volume management device) bridge; returns 0 or ENXIO. It zeroes the softc, sets the PCI domain to PCI_DOMAINMAX minus the unit and enables bus mastering. It allocates up to VMD_MAX_BAR memory BARs (stepping over the high half of 64-bit BARs); a failure prints 'Cannot allocate resources' and goes to fail. It finds the device entry for the vendor and device id, computes the bus range (restricting the start bus to 0, 128 or 224 when the device has the BUS_RESTRICT capability and the config register says so, failing on an unknown offset) and sets up the bus-number rman and the memory-window rman from the BARs (each failure goes to fail). It then sets the MSI-X handling: when vmd_bypass_msi is set and the device can bypass MSI it sets vmd_msix_count to 0 and enables MSI bypass; otherwise, if pci_alloc_msix succeeds it allocates an irq entry per vector, allocating each IRQ and setting up vmd_intr on it (a failure goes to fail) and disables MSI bypass; if pci_alloc_msix fails it neither installs handlers nor enables bypass and attach continues. It then sets the DMA tag, adds the pci child, attaches children and returns 0. The fail label calls vmd_free(sc) and returns ENXIO.
note: vmd.c:247-392 (slice 259-517 starts inside; name correct). Reviewer round 15 right: attach can succeed with neither MSI-X handlers nor bypass when pci_alloc_msix fails (360-384, 385-388). Returns 388, 392. Not read: vmd_free, vmd_set_msi_bypass.

name: get_memseg
prose: Returns information about a bhyve memory segment; static int. It calls vm_get_memseg(sc->vm, mseg->segid, &mseg->len, &sysmem, NULL); this call can write mseg->len, including on a path where it then fails. If it returns an error, or the segment length is 0, it returns that error (0 for a zero length) without touching mseg->name. For a non-system-memory segment it searches the softc's devmem list for the entry with the same segid; the entry is only asserted to exist (KASSERT, active only in debug builds): there is no EINVAL return for a missing entry, and without the assertion the following dsc->name access would use a NULL pointer. It then copies the device name into mseg->name with copystr (at most len bytes, result returned). For a system memory segment it zeroes len bytes of mseg->name. It returns the resulting error.
note: vmm_dev.c:244-267. Reviewer round 1 and round 2 right (mseg->len may be written by vm_get_memseg, 250); round 15 wrong: no EINVAL exists for a missing devmem entry, it is only a KASSERT (259-260). Returns 252, 266.

name: vmci_queue_pair_alloc_guest_work
prose: Allocates or attaches to a guest-side VMCI queue pair; returns VMCI_SUCCESS or a VMCI error code. It returns VMCI_ERROR_NO_ACCESS if priv_flags is not VMCI_NO_PRIVILEGE_FLAGS. It takes the guest endpoints mutex. If the guest is hibernating and the flags do not include VMCI_QPFLAG_LOCAL it returns VMCI_ERROR_UNAVAILABLE (this check precedes the lookup of an existing entry). If an entry for the handle already exists: for a local queue pair with ref_count above 1 it returns VMCI_ERROR_UNAVAILABLE; if the sizes or flags (ignoring ATTACH_ONLY) do not match it returns VMCI_ERROR_QUEUEPAIR_MISMATCH; otherwise it notifies the peer locally, and on success it reuses the existing queues swapped (produce and consume exchanged) and jumps to out; for a non-local existing entry it returns VMCI_ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS. Without an entry it allocates the produce and consume queues (VMCI_ERROR_NO_MEM on failure), creates the endpoint, and allocates the PPN set; for a local pair it checks the handle's context and peer against the current context (VMCI_ERROR_NO_ACCESS) and rejects ATTACH_ONLY (VMCI_ERROR_NOT_FOUND), for a non-local pair it makes the allocation hypercall; failures free the endpoint or the queues and return the code. It then adds the entry to the list, and at out increments ref_count, stores the handle and the queue pointers for the caller, initializes the queue headers for a newly created local pair (ref_count 1), releases the mutex and returns VMCI_SUCCESS. The error_keep_entry exits keep the existing entry.
note: vmci_queue_pair.c:576-756 (slice 528-779 starts earlier). Reviewer original right (priv_flags must be VMCI_NO_PRIVILEGE_FLAGS, 591-592; local attach success reuses existing queues, 638-640); round 15 right (VMCI_ERROR_UNAVAILABLE for non-local attach during hibernation, checked before the entry lookup, 596-606). Returns 592, 736, 749, 755.

name: vt_parse_rgb_triplet
prose: Parses a colour given as '#rrggbb' or as three decimal components; int, 0 on success or -1. If the string starts with '#' its total length must be exactly 7 (otherwise -1); the 6 characters after '#' are parsed with strtoul base 16 and must be consumed completely (a non-empty end remainder gives -1), so strtoul's own conventions apply (a leading sign, white space or 0x prefix inside those 6 characters is accepted when it fits); r, g and b are set from bits 23-16, 15-8 and 7-0 and it returns 0. For the decimal form it parses three numbers with strtoul base 10 separated by commas or spaces: if a number has no digits or is above 255 it returns -1 (a negative number wraps to a large unsigned value and fails, except '-0' or '-00', which parse as 0); *r is stored after the first number and *g after the second, before the later parts are checked, and *b after the third, so on a later failure (including trailing garbage after the third number) the earlier outputs may already have been written. After the third number only spaces are skipped and any other remaining character gives -1; otherwise it returns 0.
note: vt_termcolors.c:63-129. Reviewer round 1 right (strtoul accepts a sign/0x/white space within the 6 hex characters); round 2 right ('# 1234' has length 6 so -1); round 15 right (wrap-around depends on the width of unsigned long, I did not claim a width); round 17 right (*b may be written before a trailing-character failure, '-00' also passes). Returns 75, 78, 84, 90, 92, 102, 104, 114, 116, 126, 128.

name: vt_mouse_event
prose: Handles a mouse event for the vt console; void. It uses the main device's current window and font. It returns without doing anything if the window has VWF_MOUSE_HIDE or VWF_GRAPHICS set or has no font (text mode). If vw_mouse_level > 0 it first forwards the event to the terminal with vt_mouse_terminput. For MOUSE_ACTION and MOUSE_MOTION_EVENT it adds x and y to the stored pointer position, clamps it to the screen size (columns times font width, rows times font height) in vd_mx/vd_my, extends the selection mark with VTB_MARK_MOVE when button 1 or the extend button is down, resumes the flush timer and returns (without touching vd_mstate). For MOUSE_BUTTON_EVENT it handles event: MOUSE_BUTTON1DOWN chooses a mark from cnt % 4 (end, start, word, row); VT_MOUSE_PASTEBUTTON, for non-zero cnt, calls vt_mouse_paste and sets a start mark at the pointer, and in every case returns before updating vd_mstate; VT_MOUSE_EXTENDBUTTON chooses VTB_MARK_EXTEND (or VTB_MARK_NONE for a release while button 1 is down); other events return. For the button and extend events it sets or clears the event bit in vd_mstate according to cnt > 0, applies the mark with vtbuf_set_mark at the pointer cell, and, if that returns 1, resumes the flush timer, then for end, word, row and extend marks continues, else returns; it takes the marked length and returns if it is 0 or less, grows the paste buffer when needed (M_WAITOK) and extracts the marked text into it, setting the paste length.
note: vt_core.c:2387-2539. Reviewer original right (the paste-button path returns before vd_mstate is updated, 2466-2478); round 15 right (the flush timer is resumed whenever vtbuf_set_mark returns 1, even if the marked length is later found to be 0 or less, 2502-2508, 2522-2524). Not read: vtbuf_set_mark, vt_mouse_paste.

name: vtterm_ioctl
prose: Terminal ioctl handler of the vt console; returns 0, an errno or ENOIOCTL. It first maps a set of old-style ioctl numbers (_IO('v', 4..6), _IO('K', ...), _IO('c', ...)) to their current commands, then switches on cmd. Keyboard-map and keyboard-info commands (KDSETRAD after a range check, GIO/PIO_KEYMAP, dead keys, function keys, KDGKBINFO, KDGKBTYPE, repeat rates, KBADDKBD, KBRELKBD) are passed to the current keyboard with kbdd_ioctl and its error returned (ENODEV for KDGKBTYPE with no handler). KDGKBSTATE, KDSKBSTATE, KDGETLED, KDSETLED, KDGKBMODE and KDSKBMODE read or update the window's saved keyboard state, LEDs or mode, validating the values (EINVAL for bits outside the mask or an unknown mode) and updating the hardware keyboard when the window is the current one. FBIO_* commands go to the driver's vd_fb_ioctl when present; CONS_* commands handle blank time, history size (EINVAL out of range), clear history, window info (EINVAL for a wrong vid_info size), bell type, version, mode info and mouse control (EINVAL for an unknown operation). PIO_VFONT returns ENOTSUP in text mode, otherwise loads and applies a font; GIO_SCRNMAP fills an identity map; KDSETMODE switches between text and graphics; KDENABIO requires PRIV_IO and a securelevel check; CONS_SETKBD, CONS_RELKBD, VT_ACTIVATE (EINVAL for a bad window number), VT_GETACTIVE, VT_GETINDEX, VT_LOCKSWITCH (EINVAL for values other than 1 and 2), VT_OPENQRY (EINVAL when none is free), VT_WAITACTIVE (EINVAL for a too large index) and the VT_SETMODE, VT_GETMODE and VT_RELDISP screen-switch commands are handled as shown: VT_SETMODE to VT_AUTO sets VT_AUTO and calls finish_vt_rel and finish_vt_acq, ignoring their results, and returns 0; VT_SETMODE to VT_PROCESS validates the signals (EINVAL) and the owning process (EPERM); VT_RELDISP returns EINVAL when the window is not the current VT_PROCESS window and EPERM for another process, and otherwise returns the error of finish_vt_rel or finish_vt_acq. Unknown commands return ENOIOCTL.
note: vt_core.c:2581-3152 (packet name 'vtterm_ioctl (ioctl switch body)' is the real function). Reviewer round 17 right: VT_SETMODE VT_AUTO ignores finish_vt_rel/finish_vt_acq errors and returns 0 (3073-3085). PARTLY READ: only control-flow and return lines of this 570-line function were read; handlers of KDSETMODE, CONS_CLRHIST, mouse control and keyboard commands were not verified line by line.

name: vt_window_switch
prose: Makes the given window the current vt window; returns 0 or EINVAL. If a window switch is already in progress and the kernel has panicked it returns 0 immediately. It sets inside_vt_window_switch. If the debugger is active it does not take locks: for a window that is neither opened nor the console it clears the flag and returns EINVAL; otherwise it sets vd_curwindow to the window, marks the device VDF_INVALID, calls the driver's vd_postswitch if present, clears the flag and returns 0, without suspending or resuming the flush timer, broadcasting the window-switch condition variable or updating the keyboard state. Otherwise it takes VT_LOCK: if the window is already the current one it only calls vd_postswitch when the debugger is active or the kernel has panicked, then unlocks, clears the flag and returns 0 (no VDF_INVALID and no switch); if the window is neither opened nor the console it unlocks, clears the flag and returns EINVAL; else it suspends the flush timer, sets vd_curwindow, marks VDF_INVALID, broadcasts vd_winswitch, unlocks, calls vd_postswitch, resumes the flush timer, and under Giant saves the old window's keyboard state (when its kbd mode is K_XLATE) and updates the keyboard mode and state for the new window; it clears the flag and returns 0.
note: vt_core.c:566-644. Reviewer original right (curvw == vw and panic reentry return 0 without setting VDF_INVALID or switching: 572-573, 600-611); round 15 right (the kdb_active path switches without timer suspend/resume or Giant keyboard update, 577-596). Returns 573, 588, 596, 611, 616, 644.

name: vt_processkey
prose: Processes one key code from the keyboard for the current vt window; returns 0. It feeds the code to the random harvester. With VT_ALT_TO_ESC_HACK, a key release (RELKEY): for the left Alt, or for the right Alt when vt_enable_altgr is 0 (the right Alt case falls through into the left Alt case), it clears ALKED in vd_kbstate; for the right Alt with altgr enabled it breaks without clearing; every release then returns 0 without further processing. A key press of the left Alt (or right Alt with altgr disabled) sets ALKED. Without the hack any release simply returns 0. It then calls vt_machine_kbdevent(vd, c); if that consumes the key it returns 0. In scroll mode (VWF_SCROLL) it passes the key to vt_scrollmode_kbdevent and returns 0. For special keys (SPCLKEY): the window-select keys switch to the corresponding window through vt_proc_window_switch and return 0, NEXT and PREV switch to the next or previous window (modulo VT_MAXWINDOWS) and return 0, SLK toggles scroll-lock mode of the window (saving the keyboard state, enabling or disabling scroll mode and scrolling to the end on disable), and back-tab, function and cursor keys are sent to the terminal as special keys. For an ordinary key (no flags): in K_XLATE mode it sends ESC first when ALKED is set (with the hack), calls kdb_alt_break when KDB is defined and sends the character with terminal_input_char; in the other modes it passes the raw code with terminal_input_raw. It returns 0.
note: vt_core.c:876-1015. Reviewer original right (omits vt_machine_kbdevent consumption and the RELKEY/ALT-state handling, 882-908); round 15 right (RALT release with altgr disabled also clears ALKED through the fall-through, 884-888). Return is always 0 at 891, 904, 908, 913, 922, 931, 937, 1014 (all return 0).

name: usb_alloc_device
prose: Allocates and enumerates a new USB device on a bus port; returns the new struct usb_device or NULL. It finds the first free device index starting at USB_ROOT_HUB_ADDR and returns NULL if the bus has no free index (devices_max reached) or the hub depth is above 0x10, and returns NULL if the device structure allocation fails. It initializes the device (mutex, speed, mode, parent hub, hub transaction-translator information and so on), calls the host controller's device_init method if present (a failure goes to the done label with the error), moves the device to USB_STATE_POWERED and, in host mode, sets the device address with usbd_req_set_address (errors are ignored, with the address taken from the device index if the request did not set it); in device mode it sets up the USB template (failure goes to done). It then sets the state to USB_STATE_ADDRESSED, reads the device descriptor with usbd_setup_device_desc, retrying through usbd_req_re_enumerate twice on failure (a further failure goes to done). It applies quirks, and in host mode selects a configuration index and calls usbd_set_config_index, retrying through re-enumeration or other configuration indexes in several cases (including the CD-ROM and mass-storage auto-quirk handling); a failure for a device with no configurations is cleared. At config_done it registers the device on its bus port with usb_bus_port_set_device, with USB_HAVE_UGEN creates the symlink and prints the attach line, with USB_HAVE_DEVCTL sends the ATTACH notification and returns udev. At done, if err is non-zero it frees the device and all its sub-devices with usb_free_device(udev, 0) and sets udev to NULL; it returns udev.
note: usb_device.c:1752-2116 (packet name usbd_new_device is the old name; the function is usb_alloc_device; slice 1789-2078 covers most of it). Returns 1786, 1792, 1797, 2115. PARTLY READ: lines 1800-1895 (device structure setup, TT hub scan) and 1960-2085 (quirk and configuration-selection loop) via control-flow lines only.

name: wg_decrypt
prose: Decrypts one received WireGuard data packet; static void. It takes the remote from the packet's keypair and the owning peer from it, reads the nonce from the data header and strips that header with m_adj, then calls noise_keypair_decrypt; a failure goes to out with state WG_PACKET_DEAD. A decrypted packet of length 0 is a keepalive: it logs and goes to out with state WG_PACKET_CRYPTED, without trimming or resetting the mbuf. Otherwise determine_af_and_pullup sets the address family: for IPv4 it looks up the allowed peer from the source address, takes the IP length from the header and trims the mbuf to it with m_adj only when that length is at least the IP header size and smaller than the packet length; for IPv6 it looks up the source address, computes payload length plus header and trims only when that is smaller than the packet length; a packet that is neither IPv4 nor IPv6 logs and goes to out as dead. It releases the reference on the allowed peer's remote if one was returned; if the allowed peer is not the sending peer it logs 'unallowed src IP' and goes to out as dead; otherwise it resets the mbuf (wg_mbuf_reset) and sets state WG_PACKET_CRYPTED. At out it stores the mbuf in pkt->p_mbuf, publishes the state with a release store, enqueues the peer's receive group task and drops the reference on the remote.
note: if_wg.c:1612-1681. Reviewer original right (the keepalive path does not trim or reset the mbuf, 1632-1636); round 15 right (trimming happens only when the computed length is smaller, and for IPv4 only when len >= sizeof(struct ip), 1650-1651, 1656-1657).

name: wg_peer_send_staged
prose: Encrypts and sends the packets staged on a WireGuard peer; static void. It takes all packets off the peer's stage queue into a local list (wg_queue_delist_staged); if the list is empty it returns. It gets the peer's current keypair; if there is none, or if assigning the next nonce to any packet fails (noise_keypair_nonce_next), it releases the keypair (when held) and puts all the packets back on the stage queue (wg_queue_enlist_staged) and calls wg_timers_event_want_initiation(peer), so the stage queue is not left empty on that path. Otherwise it gives every packet a reference on the keypair and queues it on both the encrypt-parallel and the peer's encrypt-serial queue with wg_queue_both; a packet for which that fails is dropped (the OQDROPS counter is incremented) and is not returned to the stage queue and does not trigger an initiation. It then calls wg_encrypt_dispatch(sc), releases the keypair and returns.
note: if_wg.c:2139-2172. Reviewer original right (wg_queue_both failure only drops the packet and bumps OQDROPS, 2160-2161); round 15 right (the error path re-enlists all packets, 2170, so the stage queue is not always emptied).

name: noise_consume_response
prose: Processes a received WireGuard handshake response on the initiator side; returns 0 or an errno (EINVAL initially). It looks up the remote by its local index r_idx (returning EINVAL if not found), takes the identity lock for reading and fails if the local identity is not set. It reads the handshake under the handshake read lock: the handshake state must be HANDSHAKE_INITIATOR (otherwise error) and it copies the pre-shared key and the handshake state. It then mixes in the ephemeral key, performs the two Diffie-Hellman mixes (a failed mix goes to error_zero), mixes the PSK and decrypts the (empty) payload with its tag (failure goes to error_zero). It then takes the handshake write lock and, only if the state is still HANDSHAKE_INITIATOR and the local index still equals r_idx, stores the new handshake state and the remote index s_idx and calls noise_begin_session; ret is that call's result (so a failing begin_session returns its own error code rather than EINVAL), and on success *rp is set to a new reference on the remote. If the state check at that point fails ret stays EINVAL. In all exit paths after the lookup it wipes the secret material, releases the identity lock and drops the lookup reference on r with noise_remote_put (also on success, where *rp holds its own reference).
note: wg_noise.c:1129-1191. Reviewer original right (the result can be noise_begin_session's error, 1180); round 15 right (the lookup reference is released on success too, 1190). Not read: callee bodies.

name: xdma_process
prose: Builds a scatter/gather list from the queued xdma requests; int, returns the number of segments added to sg (n) or -1. Precondition: the channel is locked (XCHAN_ASSERT_LOCKED) and sg points to an array of struct xdma_sglist entries. It asks the DMA controller for its capacity with XDMA_CHANNEL_CAPACITY; a non-zero result prints a message and returns -1. It then walks the channel's input queue: for an mbuf request it defragments it (xdma_mbuf_defrag) when the channel has XCHAN_CAP_NOSEG or the previous segment count exceeds maxnsegs, other request types count as 1 segment; it stops when the engine capacity is not larger than (count + n) or when n + count + maxnsegs reaches XDMA_SGLIST_MAXLEN; it loads the request's data into a local bus_dma_segment array (xdma_load_data), stopping if no segments result, adds those segments to sg[n] with the request pointer (xdma_sglist_add), and moves the request from queue_in to the processing queue under their locks. It returns n (0 when nothing could be queued).
note: xdma_sg.c:561-630. Reviewer original right (returns -1 when XDMA_CHANNEL_CAPACITY fails, 581-586); round 15 right (sg is an array of struct xdma_sglist, 562, while the local seg[] array holds the bus_dma_segment entries). Not read: xdma_mbuf_defrag, xdma_load_data.

name: xl_start_locked
prose: Starts transmission on a 3Com 3c90x (xl) Ethernet interface in the non-90xB descriptor mode; static void. Precondition: the driver lock is held (XL_LOCK_ASSERT). It returns at once unless IFF_DRV_RUNNING is set and IFF_DRV_OACTIVE is clear. If there is no free transmit descriptor it runs xl_txeoc and xl_txeof to reclaim descriptors, and if there is still none sets IFF_DRV_OACTIVE and returns. It then dequeues packets while the send queue is non-empty and descriptors remain: for each it calls xl_encap into the next free descriptor; on an encapsulation error it undoes that descriptor and either stops (mbuf consumed) or sets IFF_DRV_OACTIVE, puts the mbuf back at the head of the send queue and stops; on success it removes the descriptor from the free list, links it to the previous one (software and hardware next pointers) and passes the frame to BPF. If no packet was queued it returns. It sets the download-interrupt bit in the last descriptor, stalls the download engine (XL_CMD_DOWN_STALL, xl_wait), and appends the chain to the existing transmit list (clearing the interrupt request in the old tail) or starts a new list; it syncs the DMA map for PREWRITE, writes XL_DOWNLIST_PTR with the start of the chain if that register is 0, unstalls the download engine, selects register window 7, sets xl_wdog_timer to 5 and enqueues xl_task on the software-interrupt taskqueue (to flush the receive ring).
note: if_xl.c:2444-2573 (slice 2584-2835 is the next function xl_start_90xB_locked; the old prose described xl_start_locked). Reviewer round 15 wrong: xl_txeoc/xl_txeof, the free list, DOWN_STALL, window 7 and the taskqueue enqueue are all present in this function (2462-2463, 2461-2493, 2529, 2550, 2572); the old prose was accurate. Returns 2456, 2467, 2514.
